To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we present a novel framework for joint segmentation and localization of objects in images and videos, (2) we show that our framework outperforms the state-of-the-art on the YouTube Objects and Internet Object Discovery dataset, (3) we show that the inclusion of the foreground model enables our framework to work well in the presence of similar background, and (4) we present the first framework that can perform joint segmentation and localization in videos and images.

1) we present a unified framework for video and image segmentation and localization, 2) we exploit spatial relations between bounding boxes and segments, 3) we introduce a foreground model that generalizes the framework to video data, and 4) we show state-of-the-art results on the YouTube Object, Internet Object Discovery and Pascal VOC 2012 dataset.

1) we present a novel framework for joint segmentation and localization in videos and images; 2) our framework leverages the geometric relationship between bounding boxes, superpixels and the appearance cues of the object to improve the localization and segmentation output; 3) we incorporate a foreground object model in our discriminative clustering framework to generalize to video data; and 4) we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework on YouTube Object, Internet Object Discovery and Pascal VOC 07 datasets.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: 1) How to integrate information from different representations and levels in a weakly supervised manner; 2) How to leverage the relationship between the bounding boxes and superpixel to achieve joint localization and segmentation; 3) How to generalize our framework to video data.
